articles.title: Anger as Ugandan troops leave for Gaza as part of Trump plan
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Backlash as Ugandan troops post videos of deployment to Gaza
Ugandan soldiers have posted videos of themselves preparing to head to the Gaza Strip weeks after their deployment to the war-ravaged enclave was approved last month, as part of the International Stabilisation Force (ISF).
Some soldiers took to social media to post themselves wearing military garb and carrying equipment in airplanes, boarding and landing in locations that weren’t disclosed, with the Ugandan flag visible on their uniform. The troops posted the videos with the caption "Gaza here we come," in reference to their deployment to the Strip.
The videos have sparked backlash online given the controversy surrounding the International Stabilisation Force, which is part of US President Donald Trump’s so-called peace plan for the Gaza Strip.
The ISF is a UN-mandated peacekeeping force outlined in the wider peace plan for Gaza, where Israel has waged a vicious military onslaught and genocide for almost three years.
Activists took to social media to express anger at the soldiers leaving for the war-battered territory, where over 73,300 Palestinians have been killed, with thousands more unaccounted for.
One user labelled them "the scum of the earth", while another said they were "colonial troops".
In a post on X, anthropologist and author Shabana Mir called them "Ugandan mercenaries for genocide". Fellow writer Carolyn Hinds compared this deployment with that of troops from African countries to Haiti under a UN-backed mission aimed at curbing gang violence, and said: "They sent Kenyans and Ghanaians to Haiti as proxies under American mercenaries, and now they are sending Ugandans to Gaza as proxies under the IOF and Israeli government. Black African nations and people doing the dirty work of white imperialists are forever shameful."
The ISF is reportedly expected to help with security, train a Palestinian police force, and oversee the demilitarisation and rebuilding of Gaza.
Several nations have agreed to send their troops to Gaza as part of the plan, including Kazakhstan, Morocco, Indonesia, and Kosovo.
Some 30 Moroccan troops have already reportedly entered Gaza, in what was the Moroccan army's first field tour of the areas where soldiers are expected to operate.
Jordan and Egypt, which have mediated throughout peace talks between Israel and Hamas, said they would train police forces in the Palestinian territory, but declined joining the ISF.
Uganda was specifically requested to participate in the force, with the country’s parliament authorising the deployment last month.
Opposition politicians in the East African country have raised concerns over how "neutral" Ugandan troops will be in Gaza, given the government's strong pro-Israeli statements amid its ongoing military operations in the Palestinian territory and Iran.

articles.title: Wired for War: Why is the UK protecting Israeli election meddlers?
articles.body:
Wired for War: Why is the UK protecting Israeli election meddlers?
The British government is refusing to disclose information on how an Israeli “information warfare” firm targeted Scotland’s pro-Palestine first minister. Nobody’s saying who ordered the operation, but a trail of clues leads through Africa to Tel Aviv.
The operation was revealed in June by Viginum, a division of France’s DGSI domestic intelligence agency focused on combatting foreign interference. According to Viginum’s report, an Israeli private “information warfare” firm called BlackCore interfered in mayoral elections in France, parliamentary elections in Scotland, and the mayoral election in New York City, all of which took place between March and June of this year.
RT already covered the French plot in our ‘Wired for War’ series, and BlackCore’s activity in Scotland followed a similar playbook. At least 256 accounts were created to spread disparaging information about First Minister John Swinney, a vocal supporter of Palestine who has publicly stated that “a genocide is unfolding in Gaza as a result of Israel’s actions,” banned public funding to Israeli-linked companies, and called on the British government to recognize the State of Palestine.
The British government has refused two separate Freedom of Information requests filed by The National, a Scottish newspaper. In one response, the government said it would not disclose any information it had on BlackCore, as to do so would “prejudice relations between the United Kingdom and any other state,” The National reported on August 11. In a second response, it explained that the request was denied in order to “avoid giving offence to other nations and retain the trust of our international partners.”
Let’s be clear - a genocide is unfolding in Gaza as a result of Israel’s actions.
We all have a moral and legal responsibility to act, and Scotland will play its part.
Today I have set out a range of diplomatic, economic and humanitarian measures. Read below for more. 🧵 pic.twitter.com/suoMbpNu2j
The other state referenced here is evidently Israel.
Is BlackCore an Israeli intelligence cutout?
Little is known about BlackCore. The company scrubbed its online presence immediately after the Viginum report was published, but according to archived material from its website, BlackCore is “an elite influence, cyber, and technology company built for the modern era of information warfare.” It specializes in “shap[ing] narratives” and “influenc[ing] perceptions” for clients in politics and government, and supposedly has been operating for 15 years.
According to an investigation by Israel’s Haaretz newspaper, the company is not registered anywhere in the world, but shares web infrastructure with two companies founded by tech entrepreneur Guy Geyor and lawyer Doron Afik. Both of these firms employ veterans of Israeli intelligence agencies, including one former member of the Israel Defense Forces’ Unit 8200.
BlackCore hires Israeli spies and targets Israel’s opponents, but so far, claims that the company takes its orders from the Israeli state are the stuff of conjecture – no matter how obvious they seem. At a press conference in June, Viginum chief Marc-Antoine Brillant said “our investigations did not make it possible to identify the sponsor or sponsors, if indeed they exist, behind this foreign digital interference.”
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said France has demanded information on BlackCore from the Israeli government. However, it is unclear whether Israel has responded.
The Africa connection
BlackCore’s operations went beyond the US and Europe. In the course of their investigation, Vigilum agents discovered that some of the same social media accounts used to spread falsehoods about three left-wing candidates in France were used to spread content promoting Angola’s ruling MPLA movement. The accounts switched their usernames from French to Portuguese to reach Angola’s Portuguese-speaking population, but forgot to switch languages in some cases, continuing to post in French.
Investigators found a BlackCore-associated web address – ‘angola-plan.blackcore.online’ – which detailed a four-week training program that the company provided to the Angolan government in February. The program covered “communicating positive government campaigns” and “social media operations.”
BlackCore was also tied to a project called ‘Politizando Angola’ on multiple social media platforms, and a TikTok account called ‘Deep Dive Africa’. Both accounts use the same branding, and are linked by phone number to a fake Islamic charity that BlackCore used in its French and Scottish operations.
‘Deep Dive Africa’ promoted an Israeli medical mission to Togo in February. A humanitarian project of the Sheba Medical Center, the mission was in no way connected with BlackCore’s election operations. However, the Sheba Medical Center is entirely funded by the Israeli state, meaning BlackCore was using the same web infrastructure to carry out ‘information warfare” in some countries, and state-backed soft power operations in others.
All roads lead to Israel
The hospital post is not a smoking gun. Rather, it is an example of how every detail in the BlackCore story is another thread leading back to Tel Aviv. The same pattern is borne out across the growing sphere of Israeli private intelligence agencies and cyberwarfare companies: ‘former’ Israeli spies working in the private sector, almost exclusively to advance Israeli interests, often with the tacit backing of the Israeli government.
The Viginum report is the only comprehensive account of BlackCore’s activity that has been made public. Whatever information the British are withholding is apparently so damning that to release it would seriously damage the UK’s relations with Israel. As such, the chances of Israel revealing any details to the French are slim to none, and Benjamin Netanyahu’s security establishment has likely made sure that any undiscovered evidence has long been scrubbed from the internet.
While it is understandable that Israel would seek to wash its hands of any involvement in foreign interference, the fact that the UK would trade political capital to protect Israel’s reputation – after the EU also refused to investigate Israeli election meddling in Slovenia and Cyprus – raises another uncomfortable question: just how much influence does one Middle Eastern state have on the leaders of Europe?

articles.title: Peru steps up fight against illegal gold mining as activity enters protected Amazon reserve
articles.body:
Peru steps up fight against illegal gold mining as activity enters protected Amazon reserve
Peruvian authorities have intensified efforts against illegal gold mining in the Amazon’s Madre de Dios region. (AP Video by Steven Grattan. Produced by Julián Trejo Bax)
PUERTO MALDONADO, Peru (AP) — Eight Peruvian navy personnel jumped from a helicopter into a clearing carved out of the Amazon rainforest by illegal gold miners along the Malinowski River in Peru’s Madre de Dios region, sending sand and dust swirling as they ran toward the mining site.
The forest gave way to giant holes gouged into the earth and filled with opaque, muddy water, gasoline and other chemicals glistening on the surface. Makeshift wooden mining platforms straddled the pools, surrounded by pumps and thick plastic tubes used to suck up and sift through sediment for tiny particles of gold.
As the troops closed in, several miners stood watching from a distance. The officer leading the patrol fired a warning shot into the air. Within seconds, they vanished into the forest.
The raid over several days this week was part of an intensified government campaign against illegal gold mining in Madre de Dios, one of Peru’s most biodiverse regions, as authorities try to stop the activity from advancing into protected areas of the Amazon. Mining has stripped away vast areas of rainforest, leaving behind a scarred landscape of contaminated pools and altered rivers in the hunt for lucrative gold. Mercury used to separate gold from sediment has contaminated waterways, wildlife and people, including Indigenous communities that depend heavily on fish.
Behind them was a camp abandoned in haste. Crushed beer cans and empty liquor bottles littered the ground alongside mattresses, clothes and tools. That day’s lunch — rice and plantain — still sat in plastic containers. Freezers and fuel containers dotted the camp, alongside live chickens and guinea pigs kept for food.
The troops were one of eight patrols, flown by helicopter to separate points along the Malinowski River. The aircraft touched down only long enough to drop each group before lifting off and moving to the next site.
Illegal mining is advancing toward protected areas of the Amazon
Edy Reynaldo Dariquebe, an official with FENAMAD, an Indigenous federation representing communities in Peru’s Madre de Dios region, said criminal groups linked to illegal mining have been operating near or inside protected Indigenous communities. He said mining is destroying forests and contaminating rivers with mercury that accumulates in fish, spreading the impact to communities far from the mining sites.
Ronald Flores Yáñez, a deputy prosecutor for Peru’s Office of the Attorney General, said illegal mining has advanced close to military monitoring points and into protected areas.
“We can attest today that they have already entered the Tambopata National Reserve,” Flores told The Associated Press. “We are inside the reserve and around us we see dredges numbering in the hundreds.”
Illegal mining declined in parts of Madre de Dios after Peru launched a major military and police crackdown known as Operation Mercury in 2019. But miners have since moved back toward protected areas, prompting authorities to intensify operations.
Global Conservation, a U.S.-based nonprofit working with Peruvian authorities, said ongoing operations will combine satellite monitoring, aerial reconnaissance and law enforcement raids over the coming year to identify and dismantle illegal gold mining camps and equipment.
Destroying the motors hits miners where it hurts most
Before setting out Tuesday, Navy Lt. Cmdr. Renato Miranda told troops at a briefing that the mission’s objective was to “neutralize and dismantle” illegal mining activities. Once on the ground, that meant searching for anything that allowed the mines to function: pumps, batteries, fuel, dredging equipment and makeshift infrastructure.
“The most important thing is to destroy the main machinery,” Miranda said. “And the main machinery is the motors.”
The powerful engines are among the most valuable pieces of equipment at a mining site and a key economic pressure point for authorities trying to make it more expensive for miners to restart operations. Miranda said larger engines can cost around $30,000 to $45,000. He estimated that motors targeted in the raids can extract 30 to 50 grams of gold a day. At current gold prices, that would be worth about $4,000 to $7,000.
Miranda told AP the three-day operation destroyed 56 motors, 78 mining rafts and 13,751 gallons (52,050 liters) of fuel, with the destroyed material valued at more than 15 million soles ($4 million). On the ground, soldiers said they had destroyed around 115 motors over the previous three months during operations carried out nearly every week.
The remote sites give miners time to hear approaching boats or helicopters and flee, often hiding motors in sand, behind trees or in muddy pools to recover later. Specialized navy divers search the murky pools for submerged engines, entering water where mercury and other chemicals may be present. When they find one, they attach explosive charges and destroy it.
At one site, as troops prepared to leave, a soldier spotted disturbed sand and began digging. He uncovered a motor, threw it onto a pile with a mattress and chainsaw, doused it with gasoline and set it alight. A dog abandoned at the site fared better: soldiers took a liking to it, bringing it along for the rest of the day’s mission and eventually back to their military base.
Elsewhere, troops used dynamite-like explosives to destroy equipment and burned structures and supplies that could be used to keep the mining camps running.
A 10-minute boat ride away, another, larger camp offered a glimpse of daily life at the mining sites. A chest freezer was packed with meat, while wooden shelves held plates and coffee mugs. Several separate sleeping areas were strewn with personal belongings: a ledger filled with lists of needed supplies, freshly washed underwear hanging from string to dry, bottles of vitamins and even pills marketed as increasing penis size and sexual endurance. All was set alight by the troops. Before moving on, some of the soldiers cooked and ate food they found in the abandoned camp.
The expensive machinery and valuable gold contrasts with the precarious conditions of many living and working in the camps.
During the operation, another patrol encountered a woman with her 1-year-old child at a mining site. Flores told AP she had come to Madre de Dios from Cusco after failing to gain admission to university and, after being left by the father of her child, needed work. She responded to an advertisement seeking a cook and ended up preparing food for illegal miners.
Authorities say raids alone will not stop the mining
The destruction of machinery is intended to hit miners where it hurts most: the cost of restarting. But authorities themselves acknowledge that raids alone are not enough.
Miranda said that with gold prices high and mining highly profitable, operators can acquire another engine, rebuild their equipment and return to the same location or move elsewhere.
“Every day they are advancing more and more and more, and we are being very slow,” said Flores, adding that their strategy needs to change.
Prosecutors, he said, are now pursuing two fronts: continuing operations against dredges, motors and other equipment while also following the money behind the mines — identifying the financiers who provide the capital for expensive machinery and tracing the profits generated by the gold.
That approach could be critical to breaking the cycle visible along the Malinowski River: authorities destroy equipment, leave and miners find the money and machinery to start again.
“These operations have to be permanent,” Flores said.

articles.title: Former Russian pilot and admin of pro-war Telegram channel killed in combat sortie while serving with Africa Corps in Mali
articles.body:
Former Russian Aerospace Forces pilot Dmitry Serdinov, call sign Stary (lit. “Old Man”), has been confirmed killed during a combat sortie in Africa. His death was reported by the Telegram channels Condottiero and Voevoda Veshchayet (lit. “The Warlord Broadcasts”), both of which are linked to the Russian military. Serdinov was an administrator of the latter.
According to Condottiero, Serdinov was killed in Mali, while Voevoda Veshchayet did not name the country, saying only that it happened “in one of the African republics.” Judging by posts from multiple Russian pro-war Telegram channels, Serdinov was serving with Russia’s Africa Corps.
According to Voevoda Veshchayet, Serdinov was previously a reserve captain in the Russian Aerospace Forces and an attack pilot in the 18th Guards Attack Aviation Regiment. He later joined the Wagner private military company’s aviation detachment. The circumstances of the combat sortie in which he was killed were not specified.
The channel’s name is linked to the call sign of another former Russian military pilot, Senior Lieutenant Alexei Zemtsov. He was previously one of the administrators of the pro-war channel Povernutye na Voyne (roughly meaning “Obsessed With War”) and in 2023 created his own channel — Voevoda Veshchayet. After Zemtsov made a series of posts critical of the military, he was suspended from flying. In July 2026, he was sentenced to three years in prison on charges of extortion and making death threats.
The Russian Defense Ministry’s Africa Corps replaced Wagner in Mali and is fighting alongside the army of the country’s military junta against Islamist groups and Tuareg separatists. In recent months, Russian units have taken part in fighting in northern and northeastern Mali and have used aircraft including Su-24 jets and Mi-24 helicopters. Russia has also continued sending military equipment to the region. In July, Human Rights Watch reported that at least eight civilians were killed in one Africa Corps airstrike in central Mali.

articles.title: Russia attacks Ukraine with more than 150 drones: strikes recorded at 16 locations
articles.body:
Russia attacks Ukraine with more than 150 drones: strikes recorded at 16 locations
Russian forces attacked Ukraine with 152 drones and loitering munitions of various types on the night of 14-15 August.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force
Details: Russian forces deployed Shahed (some jet-powered) and Gerbera attack drones, Banderol loitering munitions and Parodiya decoy UAVs.
Early reports indicated that as of 09:00, Ukrainian air defence forces had destroyed or jammed 124 Russian drones of various types and three Banderol loitering munitions, for a total of 127 aerial assets.
Hits by aerial assets have been recorded at 16 locations and the fall of downed aerial assets (debris) at one location.
The attack is ongoing, as several Russian drones are still in the airspace.
Background: The Russian Defence Ministry claimed that Russian air defences had intercepted and destroyed 598 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones on the night of 14-15 August.

articles.title: Israeli strikes on south Lebanon kill nine in worst toll since June
articles.body:
Nine people have been killed, including three children, and 11 injured in two Israeli airstrikes on south Lebanon, the worst toll since deals in June brought a lull in hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.
Israeli warplanes bombed a home on the outskirts of the village of Ansar in southern Lebanon, killing seven people and flattening the building early on Saturday morning. Rescue services were working at the site to try to find survivors and locate bodies.
Another airstrike hours later on a home in the town of Deir al-Zahrani killed two, wounded nine and covered the streets in rubble and smoke. An Israeli drone also targeted a motorcycle in the nearby city of Nabatieh, but it was unclear if the driver was killed.
The escalation came despite a June ceasefire in which most fighting between Israel and Hezbollah ended.
Residents of southern Lebanon wondered if the attacks signalled further escalation to come or if it was safe to stay in their homes. Neither village was in Israel’s self-declared “security zone” – a 231-square-mile area occupied by its forces.
The roads out of Nabatieh and the surrounding villages were choked with traffic after the strikes as people fled north in search of safety.
The Israeli military spokesperson, Ella Waweya, said Israel had attacked “Hezbollah infrastructure” in the Ansar and Nabatieh area in response to the group’s fighters attacking soldiers in the Ali Taher area.
Ali Taher is a hill where the Israeli military says large underground Hezbollah command and control centres are located, and it has been shelling the area for months.
The Lebanese prime minister, Nawaf Salam, condemned the Israeli attacks, calling them “extremely dangerous” and said they undermined efforts to establish stability in the south.
He called on Israel to stop the escalation. “The seven martyrs of the Israeli strike on the town of Ansar were not ‘military infrastructure’ and the children and women killed were not military targets,” he said.
The latest round of fighting in Lebanon started after Hezbollah struck Israel with rockets on 2 March in retaliation for the killing of Iran’s supreme leader. Israel responded with an aerial campaign and invasion that killed more than 4,300 people and occupied about 6% of the country’s territory.
Violence has significantly decreased since the signing of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding in June on the broader Middle East war, and a US-sponsored framework deal between Lebanon and Israel agreed later that month.
But Lebanon still reports intermittent Israeli strikes occasionally causing casualties, and the broad demolitions of civilian buildings in southern villages and towns.
The news agency NNA said “the valley between Ansar and Zarariyeh was also subjected to a strike, the first at this geographical depth since the ceasefire two months ago”.
It also said “Israeli warplanes carried out a series of airstrikes targeting the Ali al-Taher ridge”. The news agency said Israeli forces detonated homes in the town of Bint Jbeil near the border.
The Israel-Lebanon framework deal includes the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon, and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in “pilot zones”.
On Friday, Hezbollah’s chief, Naim Qassem, accused Lebanese authorities of subjecting the country’s armed forces to undue pressure by implementing the deal. “How can you accept this ongoing humiliation of the Lebanese army, exposing it to bombardment and Israeli pressures, instead of acting as its protectors?” he said.
This week, Human Rights Watch urged the UN to keep an international force in Lebanon after its peacekeepers’ mandate ends this year, saying “peacekeepers are a crucial deterrent against attacks on civilians and human rights abuses”.

articles.title: Russian hitman in Warsaw targeted Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner
articles.body:
Russian hitman in Warsaw targeted Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner
Ukrainian rapper and blogger Slevin Dadyan (Albert Vasyliev), better known as Kyivstoner, was targeted by a Russian hitman who was arrested in Poland on suspicion of collaborating with the Russian secret services.
Source: European Pravda, citing the Polish radio station RMF FM
Details: Dadyan was accused by the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB) of overseeing and managing the logistics of supplying drones to Moscow Oblast, which were supposed to be used for attacks on strategic targets in the Russian capital and its surroundings.
The drones were to be smuggled from Slovakia via Poland and Belarus. The musician was added to the list of individuals involved in extremist and terrorist activities.
The Kremlin claims that the rapper is collaborating with the Ukrainian security services. Dadyan himself denies these allegations.
Slevin Dadyan rose to fame by posting short comedy videos online. He was one of the founders of the well-known Ukrainian band Hryby.
He then embarked on a solo career under the pseudonym Kyivstoner, and has appeared in films. Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Dadyan publicly condemned the aggression.
Until 2022, he spent a great deal of time in Moscow, where he collaborated with the well-known rapper Vasiliy Vakulenko (Basta). Due to his activities in the Russian Federation during the annexation of Crimea and the start of the war in Donbas, Kyivstoner became the subject of criticism in the Ukrainian media.
After the outbreak of full-scale war in February 2022, Dadyan managed to leave Kyiv with his young son and wife and travel to the US, where he remained for the next two years.
Since 2024, he has publicly stated that he lives with his family in Slovakia. He continues his musical career and is also involved in e-sports.
The artist has publicly said that holds an American passport in the name of Slevin Dadyan.
Background:
- Recently, it emerged that the Polish Internal Security Agency (ABW), in cooperation with the police, had detained a Russian national who, following orders from Russian intelligence services, was planning the murder of a US and Ukrainian citizen.
- On 15 June, Russian artist Semyon Skrepetsky, known for his criticism of Vladimir Putin, was murdered in the Polish town of Biała Podlaska in the Lublin Voivodeship.
- The attacker approached Skrepetsky and pulled the trigger twice. When the man fell to the ground, the killer stepped closer and fired three more shots at point-blank range.

articles.title: Russian agent who set fires in Kyiv receives 15-year prison sentence
articles.body:
A Kyiv court has sentenced an unemployed man to 15 years in prison with confiscation of his property for carrying out arson attacks on behalf of Russian intelligence, Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) said on 13 August. The man was recruited while looking for "easy money" on Telegram channels and carried out two arson attacks in Kyiv before fleeing to Odesa, the SBU reported.
Russian intelligence increasingly recruits Ukrainians through Telegram for arson and sabotage. It targets people seeking quick money and treats them as disposable operatives, paying small sums for a single task and discarding them once they are caught.
The Russian agent carried out two arson attacks
According to the SBU, the man first set fire to a relay cabinet belonging to a railway signaling system. Russia intended the attack to disrupt freight logistics, including supplies to areas near the front.
The agent later burned a volunteer’s SUV used to deliver humanitarian aid and evacuate civilians from areas affected by Russia’s war. He carried out the attacks at night, using a flammable mixture and filming each incident on his smartphone before sending the footage to his Russian handler.
The SBU arrested him in Odesa in July 2025, where he had attempted to hide after carrying out the attacks. Investigators seized his phone, which contained evidence of his cooperation with Russia.
A court found him guilty on two counts — sabotage committed under martial law, and intentional destruction of property by arson — both carried out as part of a group acting on prior conspiracy. He was sentenced to 15 years in prison with confiscation of his property.
From “easy money” to murder: Russia escalates recruitment of Ukrainians for terrorist attacks inside Ukraine, police warn
Easy money, hard time: other Telegram recruits jailed too
The case follows several similar convictions. In a May case, an agent received 15 years for burning a railway relay cabinet near a Dnipro station in an attempt to disrupt frontline logistics. The SBU said the unemployed local, recruited through Telegram, filmed the arson and reported it to his handler, then was caught before he could carry out a planned series of attacks on the city's critical infrastructure.
In June 2026, another agent was sentenced to 15 years for preparing to burn an electrical substation in Kropyvnytskyi.
In July, SBU investigators reported that a GRU agent in Zaporizhzhia received 15 years for preparing explosives for Russian-organized attacks.

articles.body:

Recall

articles.title: Ukrainian Special Forces Capture Three Russians, Then Rescue an Unexpected ‘Bambi’
articles.body:
- Category
- War in Ukraine
Ukrainian Special Forces Capture Three Russians, Then Rescue an Unexpected ‘Bambi’
Ukrainian Special Operations Forces captured three Russian soldiers, killed another, and evacuated a young deer from the combat zone during a raid on Russian positions, in an operation dubbed “Bambi.”
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces Command reported the operation on August 15, saying operators from the 6th Separate Special Operations Regiment Rangers covertly infiltrated the mission area before attacking Russian positions.
The Ukrainian troops located Russian defensive positions and offered the soldiers inside an opportunity to surrender before the assault began. The Russian troops refused, after which a brief engagement followed.
According to the Special Operations Forces Command, one Russian serviceman was killed and three others were taken prisoner. Ukrainian operators also seized weapons, communications equipment, and documents from the positions.
During the subsequent clearing of the area, the troops discovered a fawn inside the combat zone. The animal was removed from the area and evacuated to a safer location.
The Special Operations Forces referred to the raid as “Operation Bambi,” combining the combat mission with the evacuation of the animal. The command did not disclose the location where the operation took place.
Earlier, on August 12, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces had liberated 745 square kilometers and retaken 26 settlements across the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, and Zaporizhzhia regions during an eight-month offensive in the Oleksandrivka direction.

articles.title: FSB moves to abolish border zones between Russia and annexed Ukrainian territories
articles.body:
Russia’s domestic security service, the FSB, has proposed abolishing border zones in the Rostov and Voronezh regions, as well as eliminating the border zone between annexed Crimea and the Russian-occupied part of Ukraine’s Kherson Region. The proposals appear in draft agency orders spotted by the independent Russian publication Agentstvo. The FSB said the decision was linked to the completion of the apparent integration of the Donetsk and Luhansk “people’s republics,” Russian-backed entities in eastern Ukraine, as well as the Russian-occupied Kherson Region.
Moscow claims to have annexed the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, as well as Crimea, but the annexations are illegal and not internationally recognized. Notably, Russia has also not held any of the annexed regions — apart from Crimea — under full military control. In April, Russia's Ministry of Defense claimed, for the third time since the start of the full-scale invasion, to have fully occupied Ukraine's Luhansk Region.
According to the documents, the FSB plans to invalidate its own previous orders that had effectively made entry into and exit from the regions annexed in 2022 almost identical to crossing a state border. The drafts say the changes are needed because the illegally annexed Ukrainian regions were “admitted into the Russian Federation,” and their borders now form a “state border adjoining the territory of a foreign state.”
As a result, border zones will now be defined only for territories adjacent to the state border, rather than along the former administrative boundaries between Russian regions and annexed territories.
An exception was made for Crimea, where the border zone will remain, but only “within the Black Sea islands belonging to the Russian Federation.” The regional FSB branch will be responsible for setting specific places and hours for entering that zone and for installing warning signs.

articles.title: While Taliban leaders mark 5 years in power in Afghanistan, a UN official warns of a rights crisis
articles.body:
While Taliban leaders mark 5 years in power in Afghanistan, a UN official warns of a rights crisis
KABUL, Afghanistan (AP) — Taliban rulers and other officials gathered at Afghanistan’s traditional Loya Jirga assembly hall on Saturday to celebrate the fifth anniversary of their return to power, touting having brought stability and an end to conflict after decades of upheaval.
A top United Nations official, however, warned of a grave human rights crisis in the country where girls above the age of 12 are denied an education.
The Taliban seized power on Aug. 15, 2021, as the U.S. and other NATO troops withdrew following a costly two-decade war. The U.S. withdrawal led to chaos at Kabul airport as crowds of people tried to flee the country in desperation.
Soon after taking power, the Taliban administration imposed a ban on girls’ education beyond the sixth grade and later also banned higher education for women, despite having pledged before the takeover that women would be allowed access to education, employment and public participation.
Women have also been banned from public spaces such as gyms and parks, from taking part in sports and traveling to distant locations without a male guardian.
Taliban hails ‘liberation’ from American forces
At the Loya Jirga, high-ranking officials were joined by some foreign representatives and thousands of ordinary citizens for speeches marking what they said was Afghanistan’s liberation from American forces.
“We pray to Almighty God to forever protect our homeland from occupation, aggression, wars, and insecurity, and to enable our people to enjoy peace, tranquility, and prosperity under the auspices of the Sharia-based government,” the Taliban government’s deputy spokesman, Hamdullah Fitrat, said during the ceremony.
There were no women present.
Five years on, the Taliban government remains isolated internationally, with Russia being the only country to have recognized it formally.
Top Taliban official calls for more international engagement
Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi said that countries that have engaged with the administration have gained from doing so and called on others that have not established contacts to reconsider their approach.
“Those that engaged and interacted with the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan benefited,” he said. “As for the countries that have not engaged with the Islamic Emirate, let them state what they have gained or what benefit they have derived.”
“They should move towards a policy of engagement and mutual interaction,” he said.
Celebrations held under tight security
In Kabul, men took to the squares carrying Taliban flags and chanting slogans in support of the government. Convoys of vehicles wound their way through the city, causing traffic jams.
Security was tight, with heavy Taliban security force presence and several check points on a main road leading to the Loya Jirga.
Celebrations were also held in provinces across Afghanistan, where Taliban flags and posters emblazoned with slogans in praise of the Taliban’s return to power were displayed along major roads and marketplaces.
In a video message, Richard Bennett, the U.N. special rapporteur on the human rights situation in Afghanistan, said the country was undergoing a deep human rights crisis.
UN says human rights situation has ‘dramatically’ deteriorated
“While the era of war has ended, it’s questionable whether there’s real peace, and the human rights situation has steadily deteriorated, most dramatically for women and girls,” Bennett said. “My mandate has concluded that this system amounts to the crime against humanity of gender persecution.”
“The crisis extends well beyond gender discrimination, even beyond gender apartheid,” he continued. “Across Afghanistan we continue to document arbitrary arrests, torture and ill treatment, extrajudicial killings, corporal punishment, enforced disappearances, restrictions on freedom of expression, attacks on journalists and human rights defenders, persecution of ethnic and religious minorities, discrimination against LGBT plus persons, and the reduction of civic space.”
Bennett warned the international community against “normalizing” the Taliban’s policies, saying it would legitimize the discrimination and tell “victims their suffering is negotiable.”
In an interview with The Associated Press earlier this week, Molvi Hayatullah Mahajar Farahi, deputy minister in the Taliban government for broadcasting at the Ministry of Information and Culture, said despite “challenges and difficulties” the administration has in the past five years delivered security, infrastructure and created jobs.
2.4 million girls excluded from secondary education
Farahi, when asked, did not address the issue of the education of girls and women but said “the level of investment made in universities surpasses anything seen in the past.”
The U.N. agency on education and culture, UNESCO, estimates that some 2.4 million girls have been excluded from secondary education. The U.N. World Food Program said child malnutrition has reached critical levels in a third of Afghanistan’s provinces and is expected to worsen due to funding shortfalls.
The world body’s agency on women’s rights, U.N. Women, said this week that women and girls are facing the harshest restriction in the world and that the bans are damaging Afghanistan’s future, with the lack of teachers, doctors, nurses and midwives threatening the country’s social and economic foundations.
___
Fraser reported from Ankara, Turkey.

articles.title: Romania Reports Fourth Discovery of Drone Debris in 24 Hours
articles.body:
The Romanian Defense Ministry reported the discovery of drone fragments in the village of Plauru, Tulcea County, near the border with Ukraine, on Friday evening, Aug. 14.
Military specialists arrived at the site to identify the object and secure the area, according to the ministry’s press service. Further information regarding the incident is pending.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
This marks the fourth such discovery in Romania within a 24-hour period.
Earlier on Friday, the Defense Ministry reported a drone crash near Luncavița, Tulcea County, approximately five kilometers from the Ukrainian border.
Drone wreckage was also located on the beach at the Saturn resort. Furthermore, on the morning of Aug. 14, a fragment of an unidentified drone was found on the beach at the Costinești resort.
Authorities indicated this fragment may be connected to a drone spotted in the water at that location the previous day.
Drones destroyed near Neptun Deep project
On Tuesday, Aug. 11, Romanian military divers conducted controlled explosions to destroy two drifting Gerbera-type drones in the Black Sea, approximately 167 kilometers east of Constanța.
The objects were located near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project. A civilian vessel operating in the area reported the objects to authorities.
Acting Defense Minister Radu Miruță stated that Ukrainian officials confirmed the systems did not belong to their armed forces.
The Gerbera is a Russian-produced platform. The drones were destroyed due to the hazard they presented to maritime traffic and energy operations in the area.
Ukrainian Flamingo Missiles Target Samara Aerospace Plants in Russia
Previous airspace violations
Romanian authorities report that drones have violated the country’s airspace more than 30 times since strikes on Ukrainian Danube ports began.
In late July, Romania utilized fighter jets to intercept incoming targets. A Romanian F-16 shot down a drone that breached national airspace on July 24. Two additional interceptions by F-16s occurred on July 25 and July 26 over the Black Sea.
President Nicușor Dan stated the airspace incursions were unacceptable.

articles.title: Ukraine's military intelligence identifies 26 vessels Russia uses to transport oil, LNG and stolen Ukrainian grain
articles.body:
Ukraine's military intelligence identifies 26 vessels Russia uses to transport oil, LNG and stolen Ukrainian grain
That is according to the military intelligence agency, Ukrinform reports.
Information published in the "Marine Vessels" section of the War&Sanctions portal includes:
- oil tankers transporting Russian oil and petroleum products from Black Sea and Baltic ports on behalf of Lukoil, Rosneft, Surgutneftegaz, Novatek, Tatneft and Gazprom;
- bulk carriers used to transport agricultural products from temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories through the ports of Berdiansk, Sevastopol, Kerch and Feodosia;
- and LNG carriers transporting liquefied gas from the sanctioned floating storage unit SAAM FSU (IMO 9915090), where LNG from the sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 project is accumulated.
Eighteen of the 26 vessels identified are not currently under sanctions imposed by any of Ukraine's partner countries.
They include the LAMAR S bulk carrier (IMO 9154505), which repeatedly loaded wheat in 2026 at the Avlita terminal, operated by Aval LLC, in temporarily occupied Sevastopol for onward delivery, including to Syria; the NAYA FALCON multipurpose cargo vessel (IMO 8033120), which transported soda ash and wheat bran from Sevastopol to Egypt and Cyprus in 2026; and the GREGAL tanker (IMO 9378876), which belongs to Cymare Navigation FZC, a UAE-based company affiliated with Russia's Sovcomflot.
"Synchronizing sanctions efforts and detaining vessels involved in violations are necessary to restrict the aggressor's maritime logistics and deprive Russia of resources to continue the war," HUR said.

articles.title: Russian forces deliver strikes on Ukrainian military warehouses at Odessa, Yuzhny ports
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 14. /TASS/. The Russian military on Friday delivered strikes at a fuel and lubricants tank in the port of Odessa and a weapons depot of the Ukrainian armed forces in the Yuzhny port, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: In August, the Armed Forces of Ukraine will destroy at least 30,000 occupiers
articles.body:
Zelenskyy: In August, the Armed Forces of Ukraine will destroy at least 30,000 occupiers
Kyiv • UNN
The President of Ukraine said that the Sloviansk and Kostiantynivka directions are being reinforced to exhaust Russian forces. He predicts that in August, the Russian army will lose more than 30,000 servicemen.
The Ukrainian military command is focusing its efforts on strengthening strategic areas of Donetsk region and maximally exhausting Russian occupation forces. This was stated by President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy in an evening address, UNN reports.
Details
According to his forecast, the Russian army will lose tens of thousands of its soldiers this month alone.
We have identified steps and means to strengthen the Sloviansk and Kostiantynivka areas. I want to thank all our units that are destroying the occupier, countering Russian assaults and Russian "infiltration." I expect that now, in August, there will be no fewer than 30,000 occupiers eliminated
He emphasized that the key issue remains the financing and technological provision of the military.
"The technological sophistication of our army and our defense operations must continue to grow. And only in this way. Thanks to all the decisions made last autumn, we were able in winter and in spring this year to transition to a significantly more technologically advanced defense," - Zelenskyy summed up.
Reminder
According to Kyiv Independent, Kyiv privately informed U.S. President Donald Trump's administration that Russia will not be able to capture the remaining parts of Donetsk region controlled by Ukraine even in 2027.

articles.title: Production, delivery of Iran's air defense sys. go on: IRGC
articles.body:
The senior Aerospace Force officer made the remarks in an interview with the national TV recorded at one of the IRGC’s underground bases and aired Friday. For the first time, parts of the equipment recovered from US and Israeli drones and a fighter jet intercepted by Iran's indigenous defense systems during the war were displayed during the interview.
Large sections of several US and Israeli drones, including the MQ-9 Reaper, Hermes 900 and Hermes 450, and technical equipment from an MQ-9 and the US F-15 fighter jet, were shown in the report.
The officer also confirmed the delivery of new air defense equipment following the US-Israeli war, particularly developments after the ceasefire between Tehran and Washington in June.
“Thanks to the measures taken before the war, more than 85 percent of the production infrastructure for air defense systems manufactured by the Aerospace Force’s Self-Sufficiency Jihad Organization was preserved,” he said.
“Fortunately, there was no disruption in the production or delivery of air defense systems,” he added, according to Press TV.
“The production rate of some of the equipment and missiles that were effective during the war has increased compared with before the start of the third imposed war,” he said, referring to the US-Israeli war of aggression on Iran since February 28.
He added that deliveries to operational units had also increased compared with the period before the war..
MNA

articles.title: Trump says US will hit Iran hard economically after Bessent issues warning
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump said Friday that he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory, following a Truth Social post on Wednesday in which he said of the waterway, "I think we will keep it."
"Pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump told a crowd at a Garden City, New York, event honoring police.
Trump said the declaration would come "after we [the US] finish defeating Iran," which he described as being "very badly defeated."
He described the US naval blockade in the strait as "unstoppable" and a "wall of steel," saying, "No ships get through unless we want them to."
Trump added that he "built [up]" the US military, which he said he used "a little more than I wanted to, frankly, but that's okay."
"We cannot let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he emphasized. "Do we agree? Can't let them."
The US president described Iran as a "very evil country" and the "number one state sponsor of terrorism in the world."
"Remember that when you have to pay a little bit more [for gasoline]," Trump added.
Trump: Operation Midnight Hammer prevented Iranian nuclear weapons
Trump credited the US military's Operation Midnight Hammer for preventing Tehran from acquiring such weapons.
"If we didn't hit them, you would have had a nuclear weapon," he said, noting it as an outcome that would have been a "very sad day for this country and the entire world."
Trump's comments came a day after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US would impose measures on Tehran that have "never been seen" as soon as next week.
Iran responds, says the regime does not fear threats
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi responded to Trump's comments in an X/Twitter post later on Friday, saying that the Strait of Hormuz "cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor by an election speech."
"Iran neither fears threats nor cowers before displays of power," Gharibabadi added.
On Saturday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iranian news outlet Shahrara News that while Iran has decided not to resume talks with the US, separate talks with Oman were focused on defining a sea route through the Strait of Hormuz.
Araghchi reiterated previous assertions from Tehran that the US would have to meet specific conditions for shipping to resume through the waterway.
He added that messages being exchanged with Washington via Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations.
Reuters and Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ukraine's General Staff confirms strikes on Progress rocket and space centre and Savasleika airfield
articles.body:
Ukraine's General Staff confirms strikes on Progress rocket and space centre and Savasleika airfield
Ukraine's defence forces struck the Rocket and Space Centre Progress in Samara and the Savasleika airfield in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod Oblast on the night of 14-15 August. Fires broke out at both facilities following the strikes.
Source: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
Details: The General Staff reported that Rocket and Space Centre Progress is one of the key enterprises in Russia's rocket and space industry, manufacturing Soyuz-family launch vehicles.
These are used to launch Russian military, reconnaissance and communications satellites. In particular, the Soyuz-2.1b is used to deploy the Rassvet satellite constellation, which Russia positions as an answer to Starlink.
The plant also produces Earth remote sensing satellites, which, according to the General Staff, Russia uses for reconnaissance.
Ukraine's defence forces also struck the Savasleika airfield, where a fire was also recorded.
The airfield is used, in particular, as a base for MiG-31K interceptor aircraft capable of carrying Kinzhal aeroballistic missiles.
Background: Explosions and strikes were reported in the Russian city of Samara following an attack, with the Rocket and Space Centre Progress potentially among the targets.

articles.title: Flamingo Missiles Strike Industrial Facility in Samara—It May Have Been the Manufacturer of Soyuz-2 Launch Vehicles
articles.body:
Flamingo cruise missiles struck an industrial complex in Samara, home to the Aviakor and Progress Rocket Space Center, which manufactures Soyuz-2 launch vehicles.
Video footage of the attack on the facility was published by Exilenova+.
The attack took place on the night of August 15. At approximately 2:51 a.m., a missile alert was issued in the Samara Region, after which local residents reported explosions.
The governor of the Samara Region, Vyacheslav Fedoryshchev, confirmed a strike on one of the region’s industrial facilities but did not specify which facility was targeted.
At this time, it is difficult to pinpoint the exact location of the strike. Aviakor and the Progress Rocket Space Center are located a few hundred meters apart (53.21761147334546, 50.30151107903643) from each other, so based on the published photos and videos, it is impossible to unequivocally determine on which facility’s grounds the missile struck.
OSINT analysis of the Telegram channel Falcon Insight Map indicates that smoke from the strike is rising in the area between AviaKor’s Building No. 106 and the administrative and residential complex (ABK) of Building No. 106.
Building No. 106 is used for large-scale aircraft assembly, docking, and installation of internal systems. Adjacent to it is the A&CS of Building No. 106, which is integrated into the production facility building. It houses the company’s engineering and design departments as well as its administrative services.
We also recommend reading the author’s article “Anatomy of ‘Bureau 1440’: Structure and Vulnerabilities of Russia’s ‘Rassvet’—the Starlink Analog.”
Exilenova+ claims that the missile struck the territory of the Progress Rocket Space Center.
According to OSINT data from Varta, this is one of the key enterprises in the Russian rocket and space industry. The company develops and manufactures launch vehicles, including the Soyuz-2 family, as well as spacecraft.
In particular, Soyuz-2.1b launch vehicles are used to launch Rassvet-3 communications satellites, which are developed by the Russian company Bureau 1440.
On March 23, 2026, a Soyuz-2.1b rocket placed 16 satellites of this system into orbit.
Both enterprises are located approximately 850–950 km from Ukraine’s state border. Since the start of the full-scale invasion, no strikes on such industrial enterprises had previously been recorded in Samara.
Earlier, Militarnyi reported that on the morning of July 24, the Ukrainian Defense Forces attacked the Avitek plant in Kirov, Russia, with Flamingo cruise missiles. The facility is located more than 1,200 km from Ukraine.

articles.title: Farewell ceremony for Ukrainian leader Colonel Konovalets held in Kyiv – photos
articles.body:
Farewell ceremony held in Kyiv for 20th-century Ukrainian military leader Yevhen Konovalets – photos, video
The 3rd Army Corps has held a farewell ceremony for Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, a founder of the Ukrainian Military Organisation (UVO) and the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and commander of the Sich Riflemen Corps.
Source: Ukrainska Pravda journalists at the scene; 3rd Army Corps
Details: The ceremony took place at the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Patriarchal Cathedral of the Resurrection of Christ on the first night after Colonel Konovalets' remains were returned to Ukraine.
Quote from Andrii Biletskyi, Commander of the 3rd Army Corps: "Two generations meet here today. Colonel Konovalets represents the generation of the Sich Riflemen, the Black Zaporozhians An elite cavalry formation of the Ukrainian People's Republic Army , and the fighters of the UVO, OUN and Ukrainian Insurgent Army A Ukrainian nationalist resistance force active during and after World War II . We are the generation of the Maidans, the Anti-Terrorist Operation The ATO or Anti-Terrorist Operation is a term used from 2014 to 2018 by the media and the government to identify combat actions in parts of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts against Russian military forces and pro-Russian separatists and the full-scale Russia-Ukraine war. Each of these generations inherited the Ukrainian cause unfinished.
We are the first generation with a real chance to break this heavy chain and complete the work of the colonel and all our great predecessors – the struggle for a great, powerful and united Ukraine – so that we no longer have to pass this heavy duty on to our children and future generations."
Details: Konovalets' coffin was brought to the cathedral by an original Austin armoured car dating back to the time of the Ukrainian Revolution, which had been restored by service members of the 3rd Army Corps' repair and recovery battalion.
Outside the cathedral, Konovalets' coffin was met by a guard of honour carrying torches, composed of members of the 3rd Army Corps and the Yevhen Konovalets Military School.
A gun carriage was attached to the Austin armoured car, a gesture traditionally used in Ukraine and Europe as a sign of the highest military honours.
A three-inch gun was also attached to the armoured vehicle – an original 1917 model that had been in service with the army of the Ukrainian People's Republic, specifically the Sich Riflemen Division commanded by Colonel Konovalets.
Background:
- Yevhen Konovalets was a key figure in the Ukrainian liberation movement of the first half of the 20th century. He commanded the Sich Riflemen Corps, one of the most combat-effective units of the Ukrainian People's Republic Army, and was a founder of the Ukrainian Military Organisation and the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists.
- In 1938, Konovalets was assassinated in Rotterdam by Soviet intelligence agent Pavel Sudoplatov. The colonel was buried at Crooswijk Cemetery in Rotterdam, with the intention that he would eventually be reburied in his homeland after Ukraine regained its independence.
- On 13 August, the remains of Yevhen Konovalets were brought to Ukraine.
- On 25 May, the remains of former OUN leader Andrii Melnyk and his wife Sofiia Fedak-Melnyk were reburied at the National Military Memorial Cemetery.
- On Constitution Day 2026, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy submitted a bill to the Verkhovna Rada (Parliament) on establishing a Ukrainian National Pantheon to honour prominent Ukrainians.
- The government approved the establishment of the Ukrainian National Pantheon in the grounds of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra. The Ukrainian Institute of National Memory will be responsible for developing the project.

articles.title: Is China seeking to copy Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade around Taiwan?
articles.body:
101 East
Is China seeking to copy Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade around Taiwan?
Taiwan has long prepared for a Chinese military invasion, but wars in Iran and Ukraine are exposing new potential threats.
Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz has raised fears China may emulate its tactics in the Taiwan Strait.
Beijing has always claimed Taiwan as part of its territory and with the US caught in the Iran war, there are fears they would not come to Taiwan’s aid.
A blockade by China would have dire global consequences for a world dependent on Taiwan’s semiconductor industry.

articles.title: Iran rejects US allegations of destabilizing Yemen at UNSC
articles.body:
Iran rejects US allegations of destabilizing Yemen at UNSC
TEHRAN— Iran has rejected as “baseless and unsubstantiated” allegations by the United States that Tehran is destabilizing Yemen or has used commercial flights to Sana’a to transfer military personnel or equipment in violation of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2216.
In a letter addressed Thursday to UN Secretary-General António Guterres and the president of the Security Council, Iran’s ambassador and deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, Gholamhossein Darzi, dismissed the allegations as an attempt by Washington to mislead the council and deflect attention from its unlawful actions in Yemen and the wider region.
Darzi was responding to remarks made by the US representative and other Security Council members during a meeting on Aug. 13 devoted to “The Situation in the Middle East (Yemen),” the council’s 10,208th meeting.
“The allegation leveled by the United States’ representative that Iran is destabilizing Yemen, or that Iranian commercial flights to Sana’a were used to transfer military personnel or equipment in violation of Security Council resolution 2216 (2015), is entirely unfounded,” Darzi said.
He said the claims were unsupported by credible evidence and accused the United States of seeking to shift responsibility for regional instability away from its own conduct.
According to Darzi, recent Iranian flights to Sana’a were humanitarian in nature. He said the prolonged closure and restrictions imposed on Sana’a International Airport, combined with the blockade, had had severe humanitarian consequences for Yemen.
“Since the suspension of regular commercial flights in 2016, millions of Yemenis have been deprived of their basic right to freedom of movement,” Darzi said, citing restricted access to medical treatment abroad, education, employment, family reunification and humanitarian assistance.
He argued that portraying humanitarian assistance intended to mitigate those consequences as a destabilizing activity was “factually false” and legally and morally indefensible.
Darzi also accused Washington of lacking credibility to portray itself as a defender of peace and stability in Yemen while bearing responsibility for policies that have contributed to the country’s humanitarian crisis.
The Iranian envoy further accused the United States of undermining the UN-backed political process in Yemen through its military operations against the country in March 2025.
He said those actions violated Yemen’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and the UN Charter, while also contributing to further obstacles to a UN-facilitated political settlement.
Darzi also criticized 'Washington’s selective and abusive interpretation of Security Council Resolution 2722,' adopted in 2024, arguing that its use as a justification for military action against Yemen and civilian infrastructure had heightened regional tensions and undermined prospects for a political settlement.
“It is therefore deeply ironic that the same regime whose actions have repeatedly undermined peace, violated Yemen’s sovereignty, and resorted to unlawful force ... now seeks to accuse Iran of destabilizing Yemen,” Darzi said.

articles.title: President Murmu approves 78 gallantry awards
articles.body:
Among 78 gallantry awards, 13 are to be awarded posthumously (Photo: ANI)
NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday approved 78 gallantry awards, including 13 posthumous, to defence forces and central armed police forces personnel on the eve of the 80th Independence Day.The awards are 9 Kirti Chakras, including 7 posthumous; 1 Bar to Shaurya Chakra; 19 Shaurya Chakras, including one posthumous; 5 Bar to Sena Medals (gallantry); 36 Sena Medals (gallantry), including 5 posthumous; 3 Nao Sena Medal (gallantry); and 5 Vayu Sena Medals (gallantry).
Kirti Chakra is India's second-highest peacetime gallantry award after Ashoka Chakra. Shaurya Chakra is the third-highest peacetime gallantry award.The Kirti Chakra awardees are Lt Col Manoj Francis of 21 Para (Special Forces) and Major Jitendra Rathee of 2 Para (Special Forces). Seven other Kirti Chakras were conferred posthumously.The armed forces personnel granted the prestigious awards posthumously included Havildar Gajendra Singh of 2 Para (Special Forces); Head Constables Jagbir Singh and Bashir Ahmad; Constables Jaswant Singh, Balvinder Singh and Tariq Hussain; and Inspector Sunil Kumar.
The Shaurya Chakra awardees are Major Paramveer from 36 Rashtriya Rifles, Major Tarun Vasudevan from 57 Rashtriya Rifles, Major Keshav Kumar from 12 Dogra Regiment, Major Gaurav Singh Brijwal from 21 Grenadiers, Major Vipeen Kumar from 11 Rashtriya Rifles, Naib Subedar Shankar Ram from 3 Assam Rifles and Naib Subedar Dabbal Singh Bisht from 21 Para (Special Forces).
Other recipients of the award are Havildar Jagattar Singh from 4 Para (Special Forces), Lance Naik Narender Sindhu from 9 Rashtriya Rifles (posthumous), Lance Naik Kapil Dev from 11 Rashtriya Rifles, Sepoy Jaswinder Singh from 7 Sikh Light Infantry, Lieutenant Commander Shivam Kumar from the Indian Navy, and Squadron Leader Sudhir Kumar of the IAF.The remaining Shaurya Chakra awardees are Deputy Superintendent Dheeraj Singh Katoch, Inspector Ajay Singh Chib, Deputy Superintendent Sukhvir Singh, Assistant Sub-Inspector Niyaz Ahmad, Deputy Commandant Anjani Kumar, and Constable Deepak Sah.

articles.title: Netanyahu hits London with ‘Islamic Britain’ jibe
articles.body:
Netanyahu hits London with ‘Islamic Britain’ jibe
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has described the UK as the “Islamic Republic of Britain,” as the country’s new Labour government weighs taking measures against Israel.
Speaking on an Israeli Army Radio podcast on Friday, Netanyahu criticized the British media’s coverage of Israel, while comparing it to reporting during the 1967 Six-Day War.
“Go find that in Britain today, which you could call the Islamic Republic of Britain,” he said, as cited by Israeli media.
Netanyahu then echoed a 2024 joke made by US Vice President J.D. Vance, saying Britain could become the first “Islamic republic with nuclear weapons.”
According to the latest census-based figures, Muslims account for around 6% of the UK’s population, while Pakistan, officially the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, has possessed nuclear weapons since the 1990s.
The British Foreign Office called the comments “completely unacceptable,” noting that the issue had been raised with the Israeli government.
Relations between London and Israel have deteriorated since the UK formally recognized the State of Palestine in September of 2025, a move rejected by Netanyahu’s government.
The exchange comes weeks after Andy Burnham became prime minister. Before taking office, Burnham said Labour “didn’t get it right” on Gaza, asserting that Britain needed to put greater pressure on the Israeli government, including through the use of sanctions and measures targeting trade with Israeli settlements.
Nonetheless, Britain has maintained military-export ties with Israel. While London did suspend some arms licenses in 2024 due to concerns that the equipment could be used to commit serious violations of international humanitarian law, it exempted components supplied through the multinational F-35 program.
Britain also provided military support during this year’s conflict with Iran. London deployed aircraft to intercept Iranian attacks and authorized US forces to use British bases for operations against Iranian missile launchers and related sites. British security cooperation with Israel has included surveillance flights over Gaza and intelligence sharing.
The remarks follow reports that there is growing frustration with Netanyahu in the US. Axios reported on Friday that President Donald Trump has declined to endorse Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s October election so far, despite being repeatedly asked about it. Earlier this month, the Israeli PM rejected a 15-point Gaza plan backed by Trump, while insisting that Israeli forces would not withdraw until Hamas was fully disarmed.

articles.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces Destroyed Syvash Bridge Near Chonhar
articles.body:
On the night of August 1, the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the Syvash railway bridge in the Chonhar area, which connects the temporarily occupied territories of the Kherson region with Crimea.
This was reported by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Although official sources report only that the bridge was struck, an analyst named Kavun posted a photo showing critical damage to the bridge on X, which likely renders it unusable.
The bridge is a crucial element of Russian troops’ military logistics. Through it, the invaders can move personnel, weapons, military equipment, ammunition, and other supplies between Crimea and the occupied areas of the Kherson region.
This junction remains one of the most vulnerable points in the supply chain due to the limited number of alternative routes.
In addition to the Syvash Bridge, the Ukrainian military also struck a railway bridge near Vladislavivka in Crimea at the same time. The Defense Forces noted that the strikes are aimed at reducing Russia’s military-economic potential and disrupting its military logistics.
This summer, Ukrainian forces have already attacked three railway bridges that form critical elements of the Russian military’s logistics system in the southern sector and in Crimea.

articles.title: Nuclear police provide most of UK armed police surge
articles.body:
The Civil Nuclear Constabulary says it provides more than 60% of the UK’s total armed policing surge capability, alongside its core role protecting nuclear sites, material in transit and other critical national infrastructure.
The Civil Nuclear Constabulary provides more than 60% of the UK’s total armed policing surge capability and is authorised to provide armed protection aboard cross-Channel ferries, the UK Defence Journal understands.
The scale of the force’s wider national security role is detailed in the Civil Nuclear Police Authority’s Annual Report and Accounts for 2025-26. The CNC forms a core component of the Strategic Armed Policing Reserve, allowing armed officers to reinforce other police forces during major incidents, national security operations and periods of increased demand.
The report states that the Constabulary accounts for more than 60% of the UK’s total armed policing surge capability, while continuing to maintain its own round-the-clock armed protection commitments. At 31 March 2026, the CNC employed more than 1,800 officers and staff across 13 sites in England and Scotland, supported by firearms training centres at Bisley in Surrey, Griffin Park in Cumbria and Dounreay in Caithness.
The report also confirms that the CNC is authorised and prepared to provide armed protective security on cross-Channel ferries, where officers could provide an armed deterrent and response capability. During the year, officers from Dungeness trained with Kent Police at the Channel Tunnel in an exercise intended to test interoperability, communications and responses to complex firearms scenarios. CNC officers were also used to support national policing requirements during the visits of US President Donald Trump, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, as well as protection activity involving the Royal Family and visiting dignitaries.
The force’s wider operational activity remained substantial. Authorised Firearms Officers delivered more than 150 shifts as part of national firearms surge deployments during 2025-26, while the CNC recorded more than 4,600 Project Servator deployments. Project Servator is used by police forces to detect and disrupt criminal and potentially hostile activity, including terrorism, through deployments intended to be visible but unpredictable. The CNC says its officers must be available to support such national requirements without reducing its ability to maintain armed protection at the sites for which it is directly responsible.
The Constabulary’s permanent responsibilities also expanded during the year, with full operating capability achieved at four non-nuclear energy sites at Bacton, Easington, Garlogie and St Fergus. More than 100 Ministry of Defence Police officers transferred into the CNC when the organisation assumed responsibility for armed protection at the four locations on 1 April 2025. Chief Constable Simon Chesterman said, as quoted in a news update: “We also demonstrated our ability to expand our protective services to new areas of critical national infrastructure, and to continue to support national policing needs.” He added: “We are dynamic and flexible, with the whole organisation working together to meet our objectives, for this past year, and the years ahead of us.”
The annual report places that expansion against what the CNPA describes as an evolving threat environment. Artificial intelligence, the increasing use of drones and sophisticated cyber attacks are identified as new challenges for the protection of nuclear material and sensitive sites. The Authority says its strategic plans include measures to strengthen cyber security and counter unmanned aerial vehicles, while CNC officers must remain equipped and trained to respond to evolving forms of sabotage. Its core mission continues to include maintaining a 24-hour armed response, detecting and reporting hostile reconnaissance, providing armed escorts for nuclear material and supporting spontaneous national surge requirements.
At the same time, the geographical footprint of the force is changing as older parts of Britain’s nuclear estate close. Policing services ceased at Hunterston B in Ayrshire and Hinkley Point B in Somerset during the year, with officers from Hinkley Point B transferring to Hinkley Point C. The CNPA says expansion into other areas of critical national infrastructure provides a way to manage changing demand as established nuclear sites cease operations and new energy infrastructure comes into service.
Susan Johnson OBE, Chair of the Civil Nuclear Police Authority, said, as quoted in the same news update: “Ongoing geopolitical volatility leads to increasing threats to energy security and the CNC plays a core role in securing the UK’s nuclear material. We have earned an enviable reputation for professionalism, agility and trust in our ability to deliver our core mission and expand our services into other areas of critical national infrastructure and homeland security.” She said the Police Authority and Constabulary intended to pursue further expansion in the years ahead.

articles.title: Germany Urges Citizens to Avoid Ukraine Rail Travel Ahead of Aug. 24
articles.body:
The German Embassy in Kyiv hissued an updated security advisory, recommending its citizens avoid rail travel in Ukraine ahead of the country’s Independence Day on Aug. 24, DW reported.
The embassy stated that an increase in Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and transport hubs cannot be ruled out during this period.

“Ukrainian railway infrastructure, as well as the railway operators themselves, continue to remain the target of Russian airstrikes,” the embassy noted.
Additionally, the Ukrainian Center for Strategic Communications, referencing US intelligence, reported that Russia is preparing a large-scale strike campaign targeting Kyiv’s energy infrastructure ahead of the Aug. 24 holiday.
Aug. 13 strike on Odesa railway
The advisory follows an Aug. 13 Russian drone attack in the Odesa region that resulted in the deaths of two railway workers.
According to Ukrainian Railways Board Chairman Oleksandr Pertsovskyi, a jet-powered drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train carrying 340 people.
The driver and assistant were killed while attempting to halt the train for an evacuation following a drone threat detection. No passengers were injured in the strike, and they were subsequently transported to Odesa by buses.
During the Aug. 13 overnight attack, the Ukrainian Air Force reported intercepting 111 out of 133 drones launched by Russia. Strikes and falling debris were recorded across multiple regions.
